CVE-2026-125335.title: Forge: Ed25519 signature verification accepts small-order public keys
CVE-2026-125335.description: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.3, ed25519.verify() decodes a public key in crypto_sign_open() without rejecting small-order points or their non-canonical encodings. With S = 0 and a small-order R value, an attacker who can choose the public key can produce signatures that verify for many messages, or all messages with the identity key, without a private key. This can defeat proof-of-possession, attribution, non-repudiation, or deduplication checks that rely on a signature being bound to the message. Keys produced by normal Ed25519 key generation are not small-order, so applications that verify only trusted or internally generated public keys are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.3.

CVE-2026-134041.title: Krita EXR File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
CVE-2026-134041.description:
Krita EXR File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Krita. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

CVE-2026-99272.title: smb: client: validate the data area in SMB2_read()
CVE-2026-99272.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: validate the data area in SMB2_read()

SMB2_read() copies le32_to_cpu(rsp->DataLength) bytes from
(char *)rsp + rsp->DataOffset without checking that the range lies
within the response actually received. A READ response with
DataOffset == 0 makes smb2_get_data_area_len() zero the data length, so
smb2_check_message() accepts a frame as short as the fixed response,
while SMB2_read() still uses the server-supplied DataLength, capped only
by CIFS_MAX_MSGSIZE and the caller's length.

A malicious server can answer the synchronous read used by the
mfsymlinks (or SFU) symlink parser with an 81-byte READ response
carrying DataOffset 0 and DataLength 1067, making the client copy 1067
bytes from a 448-byte receive object (KASAN slab-out-of-bounds; up to
16 KiB in the general case).

Clamp a zero (or header-overlapping) DataOffset to read_rsp_size, as
handle_read_data() does for the asynchronous path, and reject…

CVE-2026-99566.title: assoc_array: keep gc's cleanup out of the live tree on allocation failure
CVE-2026-99566.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

assoc_array: keep gc's cleanup out of the live tree on allocation failure

assoc_array_gc() builds a copy of the tree. Where the copy reaches a
shortcut, it allocates the copy of the shortcut with kmalloc_flex(),
fills it with memcpy(), links it into the new tree, and only then
allocates the copy of the node after it. The memcpy() leaves the new
shortcut's next_node pointing at the old tree's node, so if that second
allocation fails, the cleanup, assoc_array_destroy_subtree() on the new
tree, follows the new shortcut into the old tree, and the BUG_ON() on
the old node's back pointer fires.

Allocate the node first, and the shortcut once the node exists, freeing
the node again if the shortcut cannot be allocated. A copied shortcut
is then only linked into the new tree when the copy of its node is there
to follow it. Nothing else changes: with no allocation failing, the
trees gc builds are the same as before.

CVE-2026-99809.title: vfio/platform: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable
CVE-2026-99809.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vfio/platform: prevent read-only region mappings from becoming writable

vfio_platform_mmap() rejects writable mappings of regions without the
WRITE flag, but leaves VM_MAYWRITE set. Userspace can map such a region
read-only and then upgrade the mapping to writable with mprotect().

Clear VM_MAYWRITE for regions without the WRITE flag, as i915 does for
its read-only objects and as fixed in drm/vc4 (CVE-2026-68445),
drm/panthor (CVE-2024-53071) and commit a5edadbae57e ("ptp: vmclock:
prevent read-only mappings from becoming writable").

Note this is defensive hardening: no in-tree platform driver currently
publishes a region without the WRITE flag. The guard costs nothing and
keeps the mmap() interface honest if a read-only region ever appears.
